subject.title: doctor --fix migrates codex/gpt-5.5 to openai/gpt-5.5, then Codex app-server startup times out on 2026.6.1

question: Should `doctor --fix` retain legacy Codex routes when canonical OpenAI-plus-Codex migration cannot prove equivalent auth/runtime health, or continue unconditional canonicalization to `openai/*`?
rationale: Current policy and docs prefer canonical OpenAI refs, but this issue and related reports show shipped doctor repairs can break working Codex-backed setups; automation cannot choose the long-term migration contract or required live-proof bar.

options.title: Adopt retained-route migration plan
options.body: Review, revise if needed, and land the #93180-style plan so unsafe legacy Codex state is retained with warnings, then decide whether #89442 is also needed for the startup smoke failure.

options.title: Keep unconditional canonicalization
options.body: Maintain the current `openai/*` canonical route and require documented operator recovery or startup fixes for hosts where the migrated Codex path is unhealthy.

options.title: Fold into broader migration cluster
options.body: Close this only after a canonical merged issue or PR fully covers both the doctor migration breakage and the Codex startup-timeout smoke path.

recommendation.title: Adopt retained-route migration plan
recommendation.body: Review, revise if needed, and land the #93180-style plan so unsafe legacy Codex state is retained with warnings, then decide whether #89442 is also needed for the startup smoke failure.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Codex OAuth/routing work and broader adjacent history make them the best available owner for the migration-policy decision.
